schema_review.rationale: Register the complete 1.3.0 no-vector, Code-disabled Server chain on all three backends, preserving history, existing Source references and pending intents with projection rebuilds and read-only startup admission. Review master 464cd152: the Atomic Memory snapshot budget changes admission and buffering, preserving the snapshot digest and frozen schema/revision resources. SQLite legacy tag maintenance creates the final table name directly to preserve canonical DDL, tag rows and transactional rollback. New revision s1401 registers the frozen offline Memory archive on all three backends through the shared chain; s1300/s1400 resources and checksums remain unchanged, and archived history is preserved. Publication requires installed-release upgrade, repeat-apply, old-startup rejection, background Worker execution and fresh-schema equivalence. Optional vector/Code and older Memory layouts need separately registered profiles. Managed Processing mode maintenance uses the canonical target lock, backup providers and durable evidence without changing pc_schema_revision or frozen migration resources. Its reviewed plan binds configuration and migration ID; one transaction publishes the mode and lease invalidation, and interrupted retries reuse the original recovery point. The Processing compatibility command delegates current managed Server storage and rejects complete unversioned historical Server storage before domain writes; unmanaged domain behavior is retained. The Atomic compatibility migration delegates managed databases and recognized complete Server baselines to the shared full Server chain; legacy decision files remain limited to unmanaged conversion. Registered Atomic current repair now shares the Processing maintenance transaction, canonical target lock, reviewed backup and durable evidence; exact managed layout and authority validation precede repair, and full Server validation precedes commit. It preserves revision and immutable authority, repairs SQLite FTS helpers, and resumes from the original recovery point. Vector/Code profiles and complete native lifecycle acceptance remain incomplete. The partial Topic recovery bundle rejects pc_schema_revision before backup or writes so it cannot bypass the managed Server chain, including on unknown revisions.
